module.title: HTML Fundamentals
module.description: Learn how websites are structured using HTML and understand how web pages are built.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: HTML is the language used to create the structure of webpages.

sections.heading: What Does HTML Do?
sections.content: HTML creates the basic structure of a webpage like headings, paragraphs, buttons, images, forms, and links.

sections.heading: HTML Is Like A Skeleton
sections.content: If a website was a human body, HTML would be the skeleton that gives structure to everything.

sections.heading: Browsers Read HTML
sections.content: Browsers read HTML files and display webpages visually on the screen.

sections.heading: HTML Uses Tags
sections.content: HTML works using tags. Tags tell the browser what type of content should appear.

easyExample.title: Building Example
easyExample.content: Think of HTML like the walls and rooms of a house. It defines where everything belongs.

terms.meaning: Special keyword used to create webpage elements
A complete HTML component made using tags

explanation: The browser displays both on the webpage

lessons.title: HTML Tags And Elements

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Tags are special keywords used to create webpage elements.

sections.heading: Opening And Closing Tags
sections.content: Most HTML tags have an opening tag and a closing tag. Content is written between them.

sections.heading: What Is An Element?
sections.content: An element includes the opening tag, content, and closing tag together.

sections.heading: Why Tags Matter
sections.content: Tags help browsers understand what type of content should be displayed.

sections.heading: Different Tags Have Different Jobs
sections.content: Some tags create headings, some create buttons, images, forms, and links.

easyExample.title: Container Example
easyExample.content: Think of tags like containers. Whatever you place inside them gets treated differently.

summary: Most tags have opening and closing parts

lessons.title: Common HTML Tags

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: HTML provides many tags for creating different types of webpage content.

sections.heading: Headings
sections.content: Heading tags are used for titles and headings on webpages.

sections.heading: Paragraphs
sections.content: Paragraph tags display normal text content.

sections.heading: Buttons
sections.content: Buttons allow users to perform actions like submitting forms or clicking features.

sections.heading: Images
sections.content: Image tags display pictures on webpages.

sections.heading: Links
sections.content: Links allow users to navigate between webpages.

easyExample.title: Notebook Example
easyExample.content: A webpage is like a notebook where headings are titles, paragraphs are notes, images are pictures, and buttons are actions.

summary: Different tags create different webpage elements

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: An HTML page has a standard structure that helps browsers understand the webpage correctly.

sections.heading: Why Structure Matters
sections.content: Browsers need proper structure to correctly display webpages.

sections.heading: Head Section
sections.content: The head section contains information about the webpage like title and metadata.

sections.heading: Body Section
sections.content: The body section contains everything visible on the webpage.

sections.heading: Why Developers Follow Structure
sections.content: Proper structure makes websites organized and easier to maintain.

easyExample.title: Book Example
easyExample.content: A webpage structure is like a book where the cover contains information and the pages contain visible content.

terms.meaning: Website title shown in browser tab

lessons.title: Forms And User Input

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Forms allow users to enter and send information on websites.

sections.heading: Why Forms Exist
sections.content: Forms are used to collect user data like names, passwords, emails, and messages.

sections.heading: Input Fields
sections.content: Input fields allow users to type information.

sections.heading: Buttons
sections.content: Buttons inside forms are used to submit information.

sections.heading: Real World Usage
sections.content: Login pages, signup pages, payment forms, and search bars all use forms.

easyExample.title: Registration Form Example
easyExample.content: When you create an Instagram account, you fill out a form with your username, email, and password.

summary: Forms are used in most websites
